title: Girolamo Ghinucci (Bishop of Worcester) to Cardinal Wolsey, duplicate of 22 July 1527 (BL Cotton MS Vespasian C IV f.363, DECODE R8613)

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C IV f.363 (old f.332), DECODE R8613

plaintext.source: L&P iv 3291 no. 2 calls it 'undeciphered'; L&P summarises the mutilated original (Cotton Vitellius B IX f.127) in English, used here only as a context check.

transcription.source: DECODE full-size JPEG (6264x9206 px), read from line crops at about 3x the 1046-px overview
transcription.notes: Clean clerk's copy ('Dupplicata'), no null strokes. Glyph forms p+, h, #, m vary in value between letters; several tokens re-read on zoomed crops.

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C IV f.313 (old f.291), DECODE R8589

transcription.notes: Aligned token=value file r8589_tokens.txt (partial readings marked ?); used as key source.

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C IV f.315, DECODE R8590

plaintext.source: Interlinear contemporary decipherment; quoted in L&P iv 5300.

transcription.notes: First cipher line read token by token against the interlinear; used as key source.

documents.shelfmark: BL Cotton MS Vespasian C III f.304 (old f.303), DECODE R8476

plaintext.source: State Papers Henry VIII vol. VI (1849) pp. 552-556 prints the letter with the deciphered passages, from the contemporary decipher in the Record Office; L&P iv 2727.

transcription.notes: Count from the sub-agent's tally (845 cipher tokens, 42 struck nulls); the file mixes token lines and alignment lines, so --measure over-counts.

system.summary: Syllabic substitution: base glyph = consonant row, superscript digit = syllable in the row (homophones), bare glyphs = single letters, a small code (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Cesar, Pontifex, Italia ...) and many nulls.

diacritics.note: superscript digits 1-9 select the syllable within a consonant row; two-digit superscripts mostly nulls or codes

system.sibling_key: The same key in R8476, R8589, R8590 (all with contemporary decipherments) and R8613; used to rebuild the key. Tomokiyo's partial table (cryptiana henryviii.htm) also used.
system.notes: Split 14 Oct 2026 from the former 'superscript' target: Gilino R8572 is a different (Milanese) system with its own key and now has its own folder (targets/gilino1527/).

prior_solution.where: R8476, R8589, R8590 deciphered at the time (St.P. VI 552; L&P 5282; interlinear) and in print; R8613 called 'undeciphered' in L&P iv 3291, which summarises the original Vit. B IX 127 in English; Tomokiyo's partial table.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Tried DECODE (login required), BL digitised manuscripts and Gallica for images.
Fetched full-size DECODE images of R8476, R8589, R8590, R8613, R8572 with the login cookie; no DOC transcriptions on the records.

L&P iv on BHO and St.P. VI/VII on archive.org: R8476 = L&P 2727 printed with decipher in St.P. VI 552; R8589 = L&P 5282 with the Latin decipherment printed; R8590 = L&P 5300; R8613 = L&P 3291 no. 2, a duplicate of 22 July 1527 'undeciphered'.
Transcribed R8589's cipher and aligned it with the L&P 5282 Latin; the decipherer's diagonal strokes mark nulls.
Established the system: consonant-row glyph + superscript syllable digit, bare glyphs single letters, nulls, codes.
Transcribed R8613 in full (814 tokens) from line crops.
Applied the R8589/R8590 key to R8613: Lautrec, Avemaria, dilationem, perpetuam divisionem came out.
Extended the key from R8613's own context and the L&P 3291 summary (conditiones, duraturam, parcendum pro liberatione filiorum, milliones, colloquia ...).
Sub-agent transcribed R8476 (845 tokens) and aligned it with St.P. VI, giving the code words (Regia Majestas, Rex Gallorum, Pontifex, Gallia ...).
R8613 read to 780 of 814 tokens (95.8%) with the merged key; 34 tokens in a few single-occurrence stretches stay open.
Second image pass on R8613 P1 l4 and l6 at full resolution: 'p10 +?' re-read as p+ and ɔ10, 'v3' as y3.
With h = s (as in R8476), u8 = o, Q1 = i and nulls xi14, Z9, ɔ10, Z2: 'Et si pinguiores eis offerret conditiones' and 'nisi hec eos spes nutriret'; R8613 measured at 797 of 814 tokens (97.9%).

Split from the former combined target 'superscript' (Ghinucci R8613 with Gilino R8572), after George Lasry pointed out that the two letters share only superscript numbering: different writers, languages and keys (the Worcester syllabary vs the Sforza key R5258). Folder, profile, page and ledgers separated; earlier steps are kept as recorded.

Statistical validation (docs/_validate.py): 804 tokens, 200 types, la order 4: reading -2.135 per letter; random keys -3.26 (z 11.7); key annealed onto shuffled ciphertext best -2.365 (mean -2.397, z 14.9); annealer on the real text -2.342. Verdict: pass.

validation.notes: claimed per-occurrence score -2.135; polyphony 0.0; 10 unread tokens left out; annealer on the real text from random keys reached -2.342

outcome.method: key recovered based on plaintext from external sources
outcome.method_basis: R8613 had no decipherment; its key was rebuilt from three other letters in the same cipher whose decipherments are in print (St.P. VI 552, L&P iv 5282) or interlined (R8590), then extended from R8613's own context.

outcome.notes: R8613 97.9% (17 of 814 tokens open, scattered single occurrences; image pass of 9 Oct settled 'pinguiores eis' and 'spes nutriret'); R8476/R8589/R8590 deciphered at the time and in print, used as key material. Garbino (BnF Clair. 327) is the Ranzo code of catalogue entry 7 (vasto1527), out of scope. Until 14 Oct 2026 this folder was 'superscript' and also held Gilino R8572, now targets/gilino1527/.
